description: Experimental prerelease candidate that carries the seven stack B decisions of bsv-blockchain/dpp#177: @bsv/dpp-protocol and @bsv/dpp-profiles move to 0.3.0-beta.10 and @bsv/dpp-overlay to 0.4.0-beta.13, and @bsv/dpp-credentials to 0.2.0-beta.6, in which mapEpcisEventWithReport under epcis-vsc@1 refuses an inspection, repair or sensor reading reporting active as its published maintenance-observation limit says, and which adds the epcis-vsc@2 mapping profile with its CBV 2.0 disposition crosswalk, a parked profile the set's selection does not claim. The verification report checks token payloads against their declared profile through a caller-supplied validator; restricted tiers are disclosed per reader; acceptance records travel in the evidence package; a managed custodian writes for a holder only on a committed dpp-managed-instruction@1 record, refused as instruction-commitment-absent where an index selects the rule; the native claim names its state by outpoint and may carry evidence facets; the index contract is 0.14.0-draft, with per-publisher write tokens bound to one key and one use and self-service registration through POST /register, a wallet-signed dpp-index-registration@1 request that appends an operator-signed policy version and returns those tokens, and the registry contract 0.5.0. The custody profile is managed-custody@2: the custodian signs its acceptance and instruction records with a derived key through the wallet's createSignature, and dpp-managed-acceptance@1 records are read and never written. Record versions and the other conformance claims are those of dpp-release-2026-10-10, except that from 9 November 2026 the selection withholds the parked VSC compatibility profile and the EPCIS claims that include its SEAL mappings, and requires the narrower epcis-source-import-1 for the EPCIS source helpers. Package publication does not establish deployment readiness or product qualification.

dependencies.name: mongodb
dependencies.note: the reference persistence of the index node, replaceable

dependencies.name: @bsv/wallet-toolbox-client
dependencies.note: the application service's wallet, and from this set an optional dependency of @bsv/dpp-overlay for advertising, at the same version; npm install --omit=optional leaves it out

packages.name: @bsv/dpp-protocol
packages.role: the passport record models, signatures, custody rules, chain and evidence verification, native lifecycle claims, attestation anchors, publisher policies and portable evidence

support.notes: Depends on @bsv/sdk only and imports no Node built-in; a browser bundle is not tested and not promised.
Normative JSON schemas copied byte for byte from contracts; relative schema references remain alongside one another.

packages.name: @bsv/dpp-overlay
packages.role: the topic managers, lookup services, storage adapters, capabilities, history, evidence export, retraction and synchronisation of the index; a supported server entry point and dpp-index executable also run the HTTP node

support.notes: Server only: Node built-ins, the overlay engine and the MongoDB driver. Importing never starts the HTTP host.
HTTP host and runFromEnvironment for an operator process. Importing starts nothing; the dpp-index executable calls the runner explicitly.

packages.name: @bsv/dpp-profiles
packages.role: the industry, exchange and operator profiles as frozen manifests with generated schemas and consumer documents, the lifecycle mapping for both record versions, and the GS1 identifier helpers; the GS1 discovery helpers, the interoperability manifests, the shared evidence shapes, the declarative applicability evaluator and the deterministic passport projection; structural profile change reports and version 4 cross-field data review

support.notes: Reads its data files through the Node file system; the one runtime dependency is the RFC 8785 canonicaliser.
The manifest, identity, exchange, operator and interoperability schemas and the pinned GS1 resolver schemas.
Generated payload schemas, consumer documents and mapping inventories.
The digests every published file is held to.

packages.name: @bsv/dpp-credentials
packages.role: external W3C Verifiable Credential 2.0 verification under ecdsa-rdfc-2019 over P-256 from did:web issuers, with authenticated Bitstring Status List status and bounded did:web resolution (./exchange), and the EPCIS source helpers with the pinned EPCIS 2.0.1 artefacts (./epcis-source); the root still exports the parked VSC draft compatibility profile, with its owned context and schema artefacts, its two proof suites and the EPCIS-to-SEAL mappings

support.notes: Server only: reads its artefacts through the file system and decompresses status lists with node:zlib.
The external ecdsa-rdfc-2019 credential verifier; server only for the same reasons.
The EPCIS source helpers; server only for the same reasons.
The owned context and schemas, the pinned EPCIS and W3C artefacts and the external passport context and schema, each with a notice file naming its digest.

alsoSupported: managed-custody@1 records, read under spec/managed-custody.md section 9 and never written
owner-signed transfer (spec/custody.md section 4) for version 1 lineages

serviceInterface.note: PassportService in the reference application, whose source is not public, is the account-agnostic entry point over the writer's journal; it consumes the packages above and is not itself published in this set.

the index's HTTP contract
the report schema and reason codes
the capability document
the frozen profile manifests
the application interoperability API contract
the durable EPCIS import record
source revisions and relationships
passport-projection@1

the interoperability manifest contract
the successor industry manifest contract
the complete export part, dpp-evidence-export@1
the carried record: the token prefix, the version 3 body, the token id, the burn and the migration rule
one carried genesis and value output of record version 3 with thirteen refusals
a five-state carried lineage, twelve refusals and the burn
the verification report for nine carried evidence cases
the proposed baseline for the carried record, with every fixture digest
the acceptance record a managed custodian signs with its derived key, with its binding and seven refusals

consumers.note: the example consumer with sector workflows; package installation, supported readers and selected writers are separate adoption decisions

consumers.name: the reference registry
consumers.consumes: the packages as vendored tarballs, to be replaced by the published packages of this set
